newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi sees better earnings in current year.
newsitem.headline: Sappi sees better earnings in current year.

text.p: Sappi Ltd said on Monday it expected an improved performance in the current financial year on higher pulp prices and benefits from the weaker rand after a poor showing in the year to September 30, 1996.
Chairman Eugene van As said in the group's annual report he expected pulp price increases to pick up in the second half of the financial year.
"Price increases will be slow but I expect that they will accelerate in the second half of the year. Sappi in addition should benefit from the weakening rand/dollar exchange rate," van As said.
Sappi covered forward and missed the windfall from the 29 percent depreciation of the rand against the dollar last year.
But Van As said the forward cover taken in 1995 had been provided for in the year to September 1996.
"We will therefore have the full benefit of the weak currency in 1997 and our margins should improve," he said.
Van As said there would be a significant increase of consumption of paper as most of the world's economies were in their growth phase.
He said merchants and converters, who destocked in 1996, would seek to rebuild their inventories during the year.
"I expect pulp prices to rise for the next two years as little new softwood pulp capacity is coming on stream.
"However a significant increase in coated woodfree capacity will occur in the second half of 1997, most of it in the last two months of the year...," van As said.
He said the restructuring of its European business had been completed and it was returning to profitability after losing money during the year.

In 1995, while prices were firm, Sappi commited itself to a 1.2 billion rand investment in southern Africa - the expansion and modernisation of Usutu Pulp Company and Tugela Mill, and the rebuilding of Enstra's No 6 fine paper machine.
He said the projects were now complete.
"Each of these projects has a good return on investment and is aimed at improving quality and reducing unit costs, therefore the group will see the benefits shortly," he said.
Earnings for the year to September 30 1996 dropped 73 percent to 230 cents a share from 846 cents, while operating income fell 46 percent to 1.2 bullion rand.
